title: Automate a repeatable task with visible outcomes

scenes.title: Automate a repeatable task with visible outcomes
scenes.narration: Welcome to Resgrid Academy. In this lesson, we will automate a repeatable task with visible outcomes. Manual copying between systems costs time and hides failures when there is no recorded execution history. We will explain the features, the setup decisions, and a practical way to check the result.

scenes.title: A department scenario
scenes.narration: A workflow posts new calls to a team channel, and a custom field records the fire district on each call. Automate repeated administrative steps and connect Resgrid to the other systems you use. The examples in this series use a fictional department and are teaching scenarios, not default settings.

scenes.title: Workflows
scenes.narration: Workflows. Automations triggered by department events. Start with one workflow for a task you repeat, and review its runs.

scenes.title: User-defined fields
scenes.narration: User-defined fields. Custom fields on calls, personnel and other records. Add only the fields you must capture.

scenes.title: API and MCP integrations
scenes.narration: API and MCP integrations. API and MCP access for other systems. Create credentials for each integration and limit what they can access.

scenes.title: New Workflow
scenes.narration: New Workflow. Create an automation workflow. Have the destination systems and credentials ready, and decide who owns each automation.

scenes.title: Workflow Runs
scenes.narration: Workflow Runs. The history of workflow runs, including failures. Have the destination systems and credentials ready, and decide who owns each automation.

scenes.title: Import and migration planning
scenes.narration: Import and migration planning. Plan moving your data from another system into Resgrid. Have the destination systems and credentials ready, and decide who owns each automation.

scenes.title: Configure one useful workflow
scenes.narration: For the training scenario, work in this order. Step 1. Choose one event and an approved destination for a workflow. Step 2. Configure the workflow action, data mapping, and integration access. Step 3. Trigger a controlled demo event and review Workflow Runs for success or failure.

scenes.title: Verify the result
scenes.narration: Now verify the result. Confirm the intended action at the destination and inspect the recorded run. Test a controlled failure and document who owns retries. A common problem to watch for: A saved workflow is not evidence that its destination received data. Protected content requires the separately reviewed egress path.

scenes.title: Try it with your department
scenes.narration: Your practice task is simple. Create a demo-only new-call workflow and inspect its run. Record successful and failed execution evidence, owner, and recovery steps. Record the result, who owns the follow-up, and when it should be reviewed.
